subproblem.title: Vertical and horizontal segment estimates for a complex primitive
subproblem.statement: Let L,y₀∈ℝ satisfy L≥0 and y₀>0. Let F,H:ℂ→ℂ and w:ℝ→ℝ. Suppose H is continuous on {z:Im z>0}, F has complex derivative H(z) at every point of that half-plane, w is continuous on [y₀,∞), and ‖H(z)‖≤w(Im z) whenever 0≤Re z≤L and Im z≥y₀. Then: (i) for every x,y,t∈ℝ with 0≤x≤L and y₀≤y≤t, ‖F(x+it)−F(x+iy)‖≤∫_y^t w(s)ds; and (ii) for every x,y∈ℝ with 0≤x≤L and y≥y₀, ‖F(x+iy)−F(iy)‖≤xw(y). All integrals use real Lebesgue measure.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (F H : ℂ → ℂ) (w : ℝ → ℝ) (L y₀ : ℝ), 0 ≤ L → 0 < y₀ → ContinuousOn H {z : ℂ | 0 < z.im} → (∀ z : ℂ, 0 < z.im → HasDerivAt F (H z) z) → ContinuousOn w (Set.Ici y₀) → (∀ z : ℂ, 0 ≤ z.re → z.re ≤ L → y₀ ≤ z.im → ‖H z‖ ≤ w z.im) → (∀ (x y t : ℝ), 0 ≤ x → x ≤ L → y₀ ≤ y → y ≤ t → ‖F ((x : ℂ) + (t : ℂ) * Complex.I) - F ((x : ℂ) + (y : ℂ) * Complex.I)‖ ≤ ∫ s in y..t, w s) ∧ (∀ (x y : ℝ), 0 ≤ x → x ≤ L → y₀ ≤ y → ‖F ((x : ℂ) + (y : ℂ) * Complex.I) - F ((y : ℂ) * Complex.I)‖ ≤ x * w y)
subproblem.natural_proof:
1. For every height u≥y₀, the point iu belongs to the strip because L≥0. The derivative bound gives 0≤‖H(iu)‖≤w(u). Thus w is nonnegative at all relevant heights.
2. Fix x,y,t satisfying 0≤x≤L and y₀≤y≤t. For s∈[y,t], the point φ(s)=x+is lies in the strip and in the open upper half-plane: Im φ(s)=s≥y₀>0. Restrict the complex derivative of F to real scalars and apply the real chain rule. The real-variable function g(s)=F(x+is) has derivative g′(s)=H(x+is)i at every s∈[y,t].
3. Continuity of H on the upper half-plane and continuity of φ imply continuity of s↦H(x+is)i on [y,t]. Consequently this derivative is interval integrable. The fundamental theorem of calculus yields F(x+it)−F(x+iy)=∫_y^t H(x+is)i ds.
4. The restriction of w to [y,t] is continuous, hence interval integrable. For each s in this interval, ‖H(x+is)i‖=‖H(x+is)‖≤w(s), since ‖i‖=1. Taking the norm of the integral and integrating this pointwise bound gives ‖F(x+it)−F(x+iy)‖≤∫_y^t w(s)ds. This proves (i).
5. Now fix x,y satisfying 0≤x≤L and y≥y₀. For s∈[0,x], the point ψ(s)=s+iy lies in the strip and in the upper half-plane. The same real chain rule gives the derivative H(s+iy) for the function h(s)=F(s+iy). This derivative is continuous on [0,x], so the fundamental theorem gives F(x+iy)−F(iy)=∫_0^x H(s+iy)ds.
6. On [0,x], the hypothesis gives ‖H(s+iy)‖≤w(y). The norm-integral inequality therefore yields ‖F(x+iy)−F(iy)‖≤∫_0^x w(y)ds=xw(y), proving (ii). When t=y or x=0, the respective integral and difference are both zero, so these endpoint cases are included.
proof_key_steps: Place both segments inside the strip and the open upper half-plane.
Restrict complex derivatives to real scalars and apply the chain rule along the vertical segment.
Use continuity of the derivative, the fundamental theorem of calculus, and the weight bound to obtain the vertical integral estimate.
Apply the same argument along the horizontal segment, whose derivative bound is constant.
Evaluate the constant integral as xw(y), including zero-length segments.

audit.reason: The one-line proposition exactly matches all prose hypotheses and both conclusions, including real Lebesgue interval integrals. The bare identifier is unreserved, and the type elaborates without either child or the parent implementation. Every proof step is justified: L≥0 permits deriving weight nonnegativity at iu; y₀>0 keeps both segments inside the differentiation domain; scalar restriction and chain rules give the stated derivatives; continuity supplies integrability; FTC and norm bounds give both estimates. Zero-length segments are covered. This is a complete independent obligation with correctly empty dependencies.
